help.title: Glossary
help.intro: What the labels and checkboxes on Stats mean. Open a chart’s data table when you want the numbers.

hcc.def: How much this home’s recorded spend rose or fell versus the previous comparable period. Buying more and paying more both raise it. It is not the official consumer-price index.

notCpi.def: The Inflation tab shows the change in what you recorded as spend, not the official consumer-price index. More consumption and higher prices both raise it.

income.def: Net income as you recorded it — take-home pay (salario neto), not gross salary.

spend.def: Expense tickets already entered. Leftover envelopes are not treated as spent.

savings.def: Income minus actual spend for the period.

savingsRate.def: Realized savings as a share of income. Hidden when income is 0.

lfl.def: On: if a year is incomplete, year-on-year figures (including HCC) compare only the months that exist in both years — for example January–September vs January–September — so missing months do not look like a drop. Off: those % comparisons skip the incomplete year; absolute totals still sum only the months you created. The box turns on by itself when the latest year in range is incomplete.

project.def: Only on Overview, and only when the latest month still has reserved remaining. Off (default): charts use tickets already recorded; leftover envelopes are not spent. On: that month’s remaining is added as if you spent it, so you can see an “if I finish the envelopes” picture. It does not change other months or your books.

ytd.def: This year does not yet have 12 created months. Absolute charts still include it, with this badge.

rolling.def: Each point sums the last 12 created months, so a missing month does not look like a crash.

cagr.def: Compound annual growth of a category between complete years. Skipped when the starting year is 0.

empty.title: No months to analyse
empty.body: Stats never creates months. Open Home and create a month to start building history.

stats.openMonthNote: {monthYear} still has {amount} reserved. Charts use tickets already recorded; they do not treat leftover envelopes as spent.
